claims.object_text: early-onset epilepsy; intellectual disability; autistic behaviors
claims.quote: Protocadherin19 (PCDH19)-related epilepsy syndrome is a rare disorder characterized by early-onset epilepsy, intellectual disability, and autistic behaviors.

claims.object_text: regulates cell-to-cell adhesion through homophilic binding
claims.quote: PCDH19 is located on the X chromosome and encodes a calcium-dependent single-pass transmembrane protein, which regulates cell-to-cell adhesion through homophilic binding.

claims.object_text: 90% of heterozygous females affected; mutant males typically not affected
claims.quote: In human, 90% of heterozygous females, containing PCDH19 wild-type and mutant cells due to random X inactivation, are affected, whereas mutant males, containing only mutant cells, are typically not.

claims.object_text: cellular interference (altered interactions between wild-type and mutant cells during development)
claims.quote: the altered interactions between wild-type and mutant cells during development, rather than loss of function itself, are responsible.
studies using Pcdh19 knockout mice showed that the complete loss of function also causes autism-like behaviors both in males and females
the complete loss of function also causes autism-like behaviors both in males and females

claims.object_text: Xenopus tropicalis tadpoles with complete or mosaic loss of function
claims.quote: we generated Xenopus tropicalis tadpoles with complete or mosaic loss of function by injecting antisense morpholino oligonucleotides into the blastomeres of neural lineage at different stages of development.
We found that either mosaic or complete knockdown results in seizure-like behaviors, which could be rescued by antiseizure medication, and repetitive behaviors.
which could be rescued by antiseizure medication
Our results suggest that the loss of PCDH19 function itself, in addition to cellular interference, may also contribute to PCDH19-related epilepsy.
